claims.text: Failure modes (gap found and fixed): the importer's search for the order of lines booked at the same moment was recursive. A group of about 1,000 or more such lines, which a date-only export gives when a whole day is at midnight, raised RecursionError past the importer contract instead of being refused by line. The search could also refuse valid files: it scanned every remaining line at each step, so 300 to 500 same-moment lines written in reverse order ran past the 100,000-step cap. It is now an iterative depth-first search that looks candidates up by each line's balance before it, tries chain heads first when no balance is known yet, and keeps the step cap. Valid groups are ordered in about one step per line, and a group that no order chains is refused, never a crash.

claims.text: Security, input at the boundary: JSON is parsed with exact decimals, NaN and Infinity are refused, and so is a key given twice. Deep nesting is refused as 'not JSON' rather than crashing. A TransactionId that starts with a formula character or a space, holds a control character or runs past 210 characters is refused, and descriptions go through the contract's CSV formula neutralisation. Refusals name lines, never cell values.

claims.text: Security, secrets and dependencies: no secrets are added, and there is no new dependency (pyproject.toml is unchanged since the base).

Performance: 10,000 transactions convert in about 0.7 s, and 3,000 lines at one moment in about 0.2 s. Line lookup by offset uses bisect, and the same-moment search is bounded by ORDER_STEPS. There are no queries, endpoints or pagination.

Data and migrations: the change is additive. FORMATS gains openbanking, the Imported dataclass gains pending and repeated with defaults of 0, and the import log entry gains pending and repeated only for openbanking. Nothing is backfilled, and older csv and monzo entries read as before.

Observability: each import writes one case-log entry with format, the hashes, lines, period, pending and repeated, and the CLI prints the pending and repeated counts. The test reads those entry fields back.

claims.text: Alerting and dashboards: not applicable. The design ships no remote alerting by design; the tool refuses with a non-zero exit, and `cma case import` exits 2 on any refusal.

Operability and rollback: the new format runs only when --format openbanking is passed, so it needs no flag. Rollback is to stop using the format or reinstall the previous wheel; case folders it wrote stay readable, since the statement is the ordinary five-column CSV. There are no config or secret changes to deploy.

notes: Gaps for the owner, not changed (they need design or are outside this seat's scope): (1) Changelog: the repo has no CHANGELOG file, so no release-note line was written; the design's Consumer trace and Interfaces were not updated with the Open Banking contract (the importer contract section already describes it). (2) When lines booked at the same moment can chain in more than one order, the order chosen is the first one found (chain heads first, then file order). A different valid order gives different intermediate balances, though the same closing balance; no requirement says which order to pick. (3) The ordering search still gives up after ORDER_STEPS (100,000) on pathological groups with many balance-less lines or several valid branches, and refuses the file. (4) The probe scripts live in the scratchpad (/tmp/claude-0/sp), not under tests/; the new regression tests cover the same cases.
